headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection and data-leakage via OpenMetadata MCP/webhooks feeding Perplexity’s browser/search workflows; no direct host-execution conflict is evident.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenMetadata exposes MCP, APIs, events, and webhooks, so its outputs can reach Perplexity through shared workflows or copied content. Perplexity runs browser-based search and cites web content, which can treat attacker-controlled text as authoritative. The pair lacks a documented provenance filter, so interaction risk is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata webhooks or MCP outputs are pasted into Perplexity prompts, injection is possible.
IF Perplexity is asked to summarize OpenMetadata-generated text without provenance checks, malicious instructions may be followed.
mitigations: Strip instructions from OpenMetadata outputs before sending to Perplexity.
Use a fixed prompt template that labels OpenMetadata text as untrusted data.
Disable webhook-to-chat forwarding for unreviewed content.
Add a human review step before Perplexity acts on catalog text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between OpenMetadata and Perplexity.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenMetadata touches governance, lineage, semantics, and memory/tribal knowledge, which can include sensitive operational metadata. Perplexity uploads documents and browsing context to a vendor-hosted backend by default, so sending OpenMetadata exports or screenshots can leak that data outside the workspace. The pairwise path is indirect but realistic in default usage.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata exports or screenshots are uploaded to Perplexity, sensitive metadata may leave the local environment.
IF the shared workflow includes governance or lineage records, Perplexity can retain them in browsing context.
mitigations: Redact sensitive fields before upload.
Use synthetic samples instead of production metadata.
Restrict Perplexity queries to non-sensitive summaries.
Turn off sharing of full documents in the workflow.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on OpenMetadata exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenMetadata can run multiple instances and uses APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted with no filesystem write, no shell, and no git modification. There is no shared mutable local resource or overlapping write surface in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable API resource, write contention could appear.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks trigger Perplexity actions through a shared integration layer, race conditions may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Avoid shared mutable targets in the same run.
Monitor for duplicate updates after concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenMetadata produces catalog, lineage, and governance outputs that Perplexity can ingest as browsing context or uploaded documents. Perplexity’s answer-engine workflow may then present those outputs as authoritative unless the operator verifies them. The pair therefore supports a plausible unverified handoff, though not an automatic action-taking chain.
conditions: IF Perplexity is used to summarize OpenMetadata outputs without cross-checking, errors can propagate.
IF downstream users treat Perplexity citations as validation of OpenMetadata records, false confidence may spread.
mitigations: Require source cross-checking before acting on Perplexity answers.
Ask Perplexity to quote exact source fields from OpenMetadata.
Compare outputs against the original catalog record.
Flag uncertain claims for manual review.
requires-engineering: add automated verification between catalog and answer engine.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenMetadata is a data-governance catalog that can hold regulated metadata, while Perplexity is vendor-hosted and uploads documents/browsing context to its backend. If regulated records are sent from OpenMetadata into Perplexity, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk inference rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated records from OpenMetadata are uploaded to Perplexity, retention controls may differ.
IF the workflow includes EU PII or PHI, vendor-hosted processing may trigger policy review.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity prompts.
Use masked or aggregated metadata only.
Review vendor privacy terms before sharing records.
Document a data-handling policy for the pair.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
